chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One cannot pray (upon the deceased) with shoes on, and there is no objection to (praying) with socks.

key_terms.خُفّ: Socks (leather or fabric coverings for the feet)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing shoes or socks during the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the permissibility of wearing footwear during the funeral prayer, specifically distinguishing between leather shoes (hitha') and socks (khuff). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often contextualized within the broader principles of ritual purity (taharah) and the conditions of the leader of the prayer, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to worshippers in maintaining modesty and cleanliness without imposing undue hardship.
